assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s17.caption: Restricting multiplicity coupling makes Equiformer's Clebsch--Gordan stage cheaper while retaining all selected output types. See Liao and Smidt.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s18.caption: The dagger identifies methods evaluated with different QM9 dataset partitions. See the Equiformer paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s19.caption: Energy and force errors are reported separately for each MD17 molecular trajectory. See the Equiformer paper.
The four OC20 IS2RE splits expose whether Equiformer's gains survive novel adsorbates, catalysts, or both. See Liao and Smidt.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s20.caption: The atomic cluster expansion organizes local energy contributions by body order; MACE connects this hierarchy to equivariant message passing. See the original MACE paper.
candidate_citations: [Drautz, 2019] Atomic cluster expansion for accurate and transferable interatomic potentials

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s27.caption: The revised-MD17 comparison distinguishes models trained on 950 configurations from those trained on only 50. See the MACE paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s28.caption: Across the 3BPA temperatures, MACE reaches its low-error regime with few layers, supporting the claim that explicit higher-order interactions reduce the depth required to build local correlations. See the MACE paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s30.caption: Aligning an edge with the reference axis selects the axisymmetric spherical-harmonic column and makes the angular filter sparse. See the eSCN paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s32.caption: Axis alignment converts eSCN's dense three-dimensional coupling into sparse aligned-frame operations. See the ICML paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s33.caption: Once the filter direction is fixed, each magnetic-order column becomes a circular-harmonic channel for rotations around that direction. See the eSCN paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s34.caption: The comparison reports both accuracy and GPU-day cost, which matters because eSCN is an efficiency result as well as an accuracy result. See the paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s35.caption: Red annotations identify EquiformerV2's architectural replacements relative to Equiformer. See Liao et al.
candidate_citations: Combining recent advances to achieve the best performance (2023).

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s36.caption: EquiformerV2's separable spherical activation retains a scalar path while applying a pointwise nonlinearity to sampled spherical features from all degrees. See Liao et al.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s37.caption: Separable normalization keeps scalar centering separate while coupling the scale statistics of non-scalar degrees. See the EquiformerV2 paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s38.caption: The OC20 results show how EquiformerV2's maximum degree and parameter count change throughput and accuracy across training-set sizes. See Liao et al.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-11/s39.caption: The compute--accuracy plots compare inference throughput and total training cost against validation force MAE rather than presenting accuracy without its computational denominator. See the EquiformerV2 paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s04.caption: The QM9 map places representative molecules around a projection of the dataset and colors structures by atomization energy. It illustrates chemical diversity inside the small-molecule regime described by the QM9 paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s05.caption: The force-comparison panel retained from the lecture shows molecule-specific, atom-wise predictions on MD17 examples. The exact drawing origin in the deck is unclear; the dataset and revised labels are documented by Christensen and von Lilienfeld.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s06.caption: MPTrj covers most of the periodic table, with strongly nonuniform element and magnetic-moment counts. The counts and label totals come from the released MPTrj dataset.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s08.caption: OC20 couples diverse adsorbates and catalyst surfaces to relaxation, off-path, molecular-dynamics, and electronic-structure data. Source: the OC20 dataset paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s09.caption: OC22 expands the catalyst regime to oxide surfaces, multiple adsorbate coverages, spin polarization, and vacancies. The overview comes from the OC22 paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s10.caption: ODAC23 connects MOF structures and CO2/H2O adsorbates to force-field, adsorption-energy, and geometry-optimization tasks. The figure is the overview from the Open DAC 2023 paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s11.caption: OMat24 combines more than 100 million non-equilibrium structures from high-temperature sampling and rattled relaxations. This overview is linked to the OMat24 release.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s14.caption: The lecture's native animation shows normal modes of a periodic chain at different wave numbers. In the later eSEN evaluation, maximum frequency and thermodynamic quantities derived from phonons become model-selection criteria.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s16.caption: Changing the stored cell moves representatives but preserves the periodic relation among atoms. This is the periodic-invariance condition enforced by Matformer.
Matformer's periodic graph retains several image-dependent edges between the same atom identities. The diagram comes from Yan et al.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s20.caption: A distance cutoff retains local real-space interactions, while a frequency cutoff retains slowly varying reciprocal-space components. The source lecture uses this ReGNet diagram to motivate mixed short- and long-range modeling.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s21.caption: GNoME filters structural and compositional proposals, sends selected candidates to DFT, and feeds the results back into training. The pipeline from Merchant et al. produced 2.2 million candidate structures, including 381,000 new entries on the convex hull, through this computational loop.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s23.caption: MatterSim spans structure optimization, phonons, mechanical properties, phase diagrams, and molecular dynamics across temperature and pressure. The overview comes from the MatterSim paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s24.caption: Open and generated structures seed MatterSim; uncertainty selection connects both ground-state and off-equilibrium exploration to a first-principles supervisor. The workflow comes from Yang et al.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s25.caption: MatterSim predictions are passed into phonon, elasticity, free-energy, and phase-boundary calculations. These panels from the source paper show the model-to-observable handoff that a static force MAE alone cannot test.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s26.caption: Rapid heating drives representative systems through large structural changes while MatterSim tracks energy and pressure or temperature. The panels from the MatterSim robustness study test behavior far from relaxed crystals.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s27.caption: Targeted first-principles labels reduce force error and improve structural distributions along a new trajectory. The active-learning result comes from MatterSim.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s29.caption: Orb's diffusion pretraining turns a disordered atomic configuration into a structured material across denoising steps. The source figure comes from Neumann et al.
Orb adopts an attention-augmented Graph Network-based Simulator rather than a steerable tensor-product network. The architecture panel is retained from the Orb paper.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s30.caption: The source lecture's native Orb chart compares system-level Matbench Discovery F1. Orb is highest among the four displayed releases; the paper also reports MPTrj-controlled comparisons.
Runtime grows with system size for every model, but the three Orb variants remain below MACE in the displayed one-A100 test. The chart comes from the Orb evaluation.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s31.caption: In the controlled rigid-body study, both models follow compute scaling laws, but the equivariant Transformer has lower loss at every tested compute budget. Data augmentation closes much of the non-equivariant model's data-efficiency gap. Panels from Brehmer et al.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s33.caption: SevenNet communicates coordinates and atom types, then hidden features between message-passing stages. Reverse communication combines partial energy gradients and forces across subdomains. The algorithm is from Park et al.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s34.caption: SevenNet simulates a 10.6 nm amorphous silicon-nitride cell and recovers its radial and angular distributions. This result from the SevenNet paper connects parallel execution to a system larger than the training structures.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s35.caption: eSEN predicts a scalar energy through stacked edgewise and nodewise blocks; forces and stress are obtained by differentiation. The architecture panel comes from Fu et al.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-12/s37.caption: eSEN's energy-conservation tests separate non-conservative direct forces, representation discretization, and nonsmooth potential choices. The plots from the source paper show that test-set MAE alone misses these failures.
candidate_citations: various tasks (2025.03).

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-13/s08.caption: Five Brownian paths begin at the same point but separate under independent Gaussian increments. Their jaggedness persists at every temporal resolution; exact plot from Dennis Sun's Introduction to Probability, Lesson 49, reused from the 2025 GDL lecture.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-14/s06.caption: Langevin trajectories follow the energy gradient while Brownian increments spread them; the empirical histogram approaches the prescribed stationary density. Lecture illustration by the author; the density-level calculation uses the Fokker--Planck equation.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-14/s07.caption: The forward SDE carries data toward a tractable noise law. The continuous-time score-based formulation is developed by Song et al. (2021); author lecture diagram.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-14/s08.caption: The reverse-time drift adds a score correction so that the process follows the forward marginals in reverse. See Song et al. (2021) for the SDE formulation; author lecture diagram.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-14/s17.caption: Flow matching transports the source \(p\) at \(t=0\) to the target \(q\) at \(t=1\). Diagram from the lecture's treatment of Flow Matching Guide and Code.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-14/s18.caption: The conditional path and conditional velocity are designed for one endpoint; marginalization produces the aggregate path and velocity. Figure from Flow Matching Guide and Code.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-14/s20.caption: Conditioning on \(X_1=x_1\) produces a Gaussian path whose mean moves toward \(x_1\) while its variance contracts. Figure from Flow Matching Guide and Code,.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-14/s23.caption: The marginalization identity works for target, source, or endpoint-pair conditioning; what changes is the tractable conditional path supplied to training. Figure from Flow Matching Guide and Code.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-14/s26.caption: Conditional paths make the lower row tractable; push-forward, differentiation, continuity, marginalization, and conditional expectation connect it to the marginal flow above. Figure from Flow Matching Guide and Code.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s05.caption: A velocity field generates a flow map, and the flow map pushes the base density along a probability path.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s06.caption: Tractable endpoint-conditioned paths marginalize to the target probability path.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s09.caption: Flow matching permits richer conditions than a single endpoint, provided their conditional paths marginalize correctly.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s11.caption: Scientific data often obey geometric constraints that ordinary vector addition ignores.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s12.caption: Extrinsic coordinates may contain the data while the admissible configurations remain a curved manifold.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s17.caption: Geodesics provide the manifold analogue of straight conditional paths.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s18.caption: The regression target is tangent-valued and its norm is evaluated with the Riemannian metric.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s19.caption: A manifold can be globally non-Euclidean while every sufficiently small patch looks Euclidean.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s20.caption: Charts create local Euclidean coordinates without flattening the entire manifold at once.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s22.caption: An extrinsic representation stores manifold points in an ambient Euclidean space with constraints.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s23.caption: Intrinsic coordinates move computation into a chart, but no single chart must cover every point.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s24.caption: Global coordinates can be useful while still carrying singularities and identifications.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s27.caption: A tangent vector records infinitesimal change through its action on smooth functions.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s30.caption: Velocity parameterizations differ in where they enforce membership in the tangent space.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s33.caption: The metric, not merely the point set, determines lengths and angles on a Riemannian manifold.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s35.caption: The metric is the computational device for tangent norms and angles.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s39.caption: A Riemannian distance turns Euclidean flow and diffusion losses into geometry-aware objectives.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s40.caption: Manifold inference cannot use unconstrained coordinate addition as its state update.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s42.caption: Exp, Log, and parallel transport provide the basic movement operations absent from a generic manifold.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s43.caption: The exponential map is the geometry-aware replacement for adding a displacement to a point.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s44.caption: The logarithmic map expresses a nearby endpoint as a tangent displacement from its base point.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s45.caption: Parallel transport compares tangent vectors at different base points without leaving the geometry.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s46.caption: Replacing subtraction by the logarithmic map gives the target velocity on Euclidean space and on rotations.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s47.caption: Manifold solvers take tangent-space increments and return to the state space with the exponential map.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s50.caption: The Riemannian gradient is metric-dual to the differential and equals the inverse metric times the coordinate gradient.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s52.caption: The determinant of the metric accounts for how coordinate volume changes across the manifold.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s53.caption: Straight interpolation and subtraction become a geodesic path and a logarithmic-map velocity.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-15/s54.caption: Geometric inference integrates a tangent ODE and a Riemannian divergence correction along the same path.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s05.caption: A protein combines a shared polypeptide backbone with residue-specific side chains. Backbone frames and side-chain torsions therefore occupy different geometric state spaces. Lecture diagram by the author.
A structure generator transports an initially disordered state through geometric intermediates toward a coherent protein structure. The intermediate structures make geometric denoising visible.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s06.caption: The AlphaFold2 pipeline couples sequence, MSA, template, pair, and geometric structure representations, with recycling between predictions. From Jumper et al. (2021).

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s07.caption: An atlas represents a curved space through overlapping local coordinate patches. Each chart maps one patch into Euclidean coordinates without claiming that the manifold is globally flat. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s08.caption: On an overlap, the transition map carries coordinates from one chart to another. Smooth compatibility makes calculus independent of which local coordinate system is used. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s09.caption: The tangent plane contains the instantaneous directions available at a point on the sphere. Its vectors form a linear space even though the sphere itself does not. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s11.caption: A tangent vector at (p) initializes a surface curve (gamma). On a Riemannian manifold, the geodesic is the local replacement for a straight Euclidean trajectory. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s12.caption: The exponential map sends a tangent displacement at (p) to the endpoint reached along its geodesic. In flat space, the same operation is ordinary vector addition. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s13.caption: The logarithmic map expresses a nearby endpoint (q) as a tangent displacement based at (p). Its uniqueness is restricted to the region before geodesics become ambiguous. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s14.caption: A flow map transports samples from a simple source law (p) to a target law (q) while defining intermediate distributions. From the NeurIPS 2024 Flow Matching tutorial.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s15.caption: Conditional paths and fields are easy to construct for a fixed endpoint; posterior averaging produces the marginal path and field. From the NeurIPS 2024 Flow Matching tutorial.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s16.caption: Pair conditioning only needs a coupling with the correct endpoint marginals. The source law may be hard to evaluate even when paired samples are available. From the NeurIPS 2024 Flow Matching tutorial.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s17.caption: The conditional and marginal constructions are connected by differentiation, ODE integration, continuity, posterior expectation, and marginalization. The learned regression target uses the lower conditional route to recover the upper marginal velocity. From the NeurIPS 2024 Flow Matching tutorial.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s19.caption: Riemannian flow matching replaces straight conditional paths by geodesics. On manifolds with closed-form exponential and logarithmic maps, the path and target velocity can be evaluated without simulating a stochastic bridge. From Chen and Lipman (2023).

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s21.caption: A manifold integrator advances through local tangent updates while the state remains on the curved space. The same intrinsic trajectory can be represented in several charts. From Chen and Lipman (2023).

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s23.caption: At the current point (x_t), the conditional field lies in (T_{x_t}mathcal M) and points along the remaining geodesic to (x_1). A different path around the manifold would imply a different conditional field. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s26.caption: A molecular generator may transport three-dimensional geometry and categorical atom identities on the same continuous clock. The geometric component can use a flow, while the discrete component uses simplex dynamics or a CTMC. From the NeurIPS 2024 Flow Matching tutorial.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s27.caption: A discrete example is a point in a product vocabulary, not a coordinate in a continuous plane. Nearby placement in the diagram is illustrative; the CTMC is defined by transition rates rather than Euclidean distance. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s28.caption: A CTMC rate field assigns an outgoing jump rate from the current state (x) to every possible destination (y). The diagonal coefficient balances the total outward rate. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-16/s34.caption: A full generator can jump from (x) to any state. The factorized generator keeps only one-coordinate jumps, reducing an exponential destination space to coordinate-level vocabulary outputs. From the NeurIPS 2024 Flow Matching tutorial.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s04.caption: The three flow-matching domains developed earlier in the lecture series. Euclidean and manifold states move continuously, whereas a discrete state changes by jumps. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s05.caption: Flow, diffusion, jump, and CTMC trajectories require different local update rules. Generator matching treats them as members of one continuous-time Markov family. Lecture diagram by the author.

A multimodal state can contain discrete and continuous coordinates at the same time. Each coordinate can use its natural Markov mechanism while sharing one joint process. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s06.caption: The generator is an infinitesimal description of a Markov process. Under the regularity assumptions used in the lecture, either side determines the other. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s08.caption: The initial distribution tells us where the process begins, and the transition kernels propagate every current state through finite time. Together they determine the Markov process. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s17.caption: The marginal generator combines many conditional paths, while one conditional generator targets a fixed endpoint. Their connection is a posterior expectation over conditions. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s19.caption: Three applications assembled in the lecture: a discrete probability flow, adjustable CTMC path stochasticity, and joint sequence--structure protein generation. The multimodal construction follows Campbell et al. and the generator superposition follows Holderrieth et al.

Protein backbone samples embedded in the generator-matching lecture. Their role is to show the structured continuous output paired with the discrete sequence modality in the benchmark above. From Holderrieth et al.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s21.caption: The four objects in conditional flow matching: a conditional path, its mixture, a conditional velocity, and the posterior-averaged marginal velocity. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s22.caption: Target, source, and endpoint-pair conditioning all recover the same required boundary marginals when their conditional paths are averaged. Lecture diagram by the author.

Flow matching can pair samples from a source whose density is intractable. The conditional path needs endpoint samples and a tractable local construction, not a closed-form prior density. Lecture illustration by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s23.caption: A coupling decides which source sample travels to which target sample. The endpoint marginals constrain the number of samples on each side but do not uniquely determine the connecting lines. Lecture diagram by the author.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s24.caption: Different endpoint couplings can induce very different path geometry between the same marginals. The right-hand transport removes many avoidable crossings. From Pooladian et al.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s25.caption: Minibatch optimal transport keeps the empirical source and target marginals while replacing independent pairing with a minimum-cost permutation. Lecture figure following Pooladian et al.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s26.caption: Larger batches lower the finite matching cost, but most of the reduction occurs early. The lecture relates this behavior to Pooladian et al., Tong et al., and the protein application of Bose et al.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-17/s27.caption: The target molecule has its own orbit of equivalent representatives. Comparing the two orbits avoids making an arbitrary stored orientation part of the transport problem.
One molecular endpoint has an orbit of rotated coordinate representatives. The group preserves the repeated molecular image and the transformation arrows from the lecture.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s04.caption: Protein function spans cellular machinery and therapeutic intervention.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s05.caption: Modern protein design relies on distinct advances in folding, representation learning, sequence design, and structure generation.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s06.caption: Programmable design aims to invert the usual sequence-to-function direction.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s07.caption: Amino-acid identity supplies local chemistry along a common peptide backbone.
Primary structure supplies an ordered peptide polymer before any three-dimensional folding is considered.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s08.caption: Protein organization turns a one-dimensional sequence into local motifs, a three-dimensional fold, and assemblies.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s09.caption: Backbone connectivity and torsion angles organize the local geometry on which side-chain chemistry acts.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s10.caption: Protein function often depends on an ensemble of conformations and transitions between them.
The transporter's ordered conformational changes make the distinction between a folded structure and a functional cycle concrete.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s11.caption: Template-based inference and force-field simulation supplied complementary but limited routes to protein structure and motion.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s12.caption: Sequence and structure databases differ greatly in scale and in the information they provide.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s13.caption: Sequence, evolutionary relations, structure, and dynamics expose different protein information.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s14.caption: MSAs turn protein families into evidence about conserved and co-evolving residues.
Evolutionary conservation matters because changing a constrained site can alter structure or eliminate function.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s15.caption: Protein language models transfer token-level context into representations for prediction and design.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s16.caption: Three-dimensional encoders choose which geometric entities and relations become learnable features.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s17.caption: Folding transforms one- and two-dimensional evidence into a three-dimensional structure.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s18.caption: Dynamics models target conformational distributions or transitions rather than one folded coordinate set.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s19.caption: Sequence design either generates a chain directly or conditions on a desired structure.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s20.caption: Structure generators propose new backbone geometries rather than predicting the fold of a fixed sequence.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s22.caption: Protein representation learning begins from an asymmetric supply of sequences and structures.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s23.caption: Self-supervision treats amino-acid recovery as the pretraining signal.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s24.caption: One pretrained sequence representation can be queried by several task-specific heads.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s25.caption: Autoregressive conditioning steers sequence generation toward specified protein families.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s28.caption: Axial attention separates within-sequence context from across-homologue evidence.
candidate_citations: Rao et al. “MSA Transformer.” ICML, 2021.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s29.caption: Protein function depends on geometric arrangements that support catalysis, recognition, and binding.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s30.caption: Coordinates alone do not encode the residue arrangement and relations of a protein chain.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s31.caption: A relational protein graph preserves both covalent order and nonlocal spatial contacts.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s32.caption: Pretraining constructs related structural views and asks the encoder to recognize their shared protein information.
candidate_citations: Zhang et al. “Protein Representation Learning by Geometric Structure Pretraining.” ICLR, 2023.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-18/s33.caption: Diffusion trajectories turn conformational perturbations into a protein-encoder pretraining signal.
candidate_citations: Zhang et al. “Pre-Training Protein Encoder via Siamese Sequence-Structure Diffusion Trajectory Prediction.” NeurIPS, 2023.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s03.caption: The database-driven paradigm supplements intuition, experiment, and simulation with reusable data and learned models. Both routes still end with candidate materials that require physical validation.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s04.caption: Material classes carry different bonding, structural, and processing priors. A model designed for a periodic ceramic crystal does not automatically describe a polymer chain or a heterogeneous composite. Original source not identified.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s05.caption: Band occupancy and gap size distinguish conducting, semiconducting, and insulating regimes. The metal has overlapping occupied and available states; the semiconductor and insulator separate them by progressively larger gaps.
evidence: Byte-for-byte duplicate of assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-03/s51-band-gap-comparison.png; source audit inherited.
The metal/insulator/semiconductor band layouts and labels match the Commons SVG by Inductiveload.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s06.caption: An OLED is a layered material system, not a single emitter molecule. Holes and electrons enter through different transport layers and recombine in the emissive layer, so both energy-level alignment and device structure control the optical output.
evidence: Byte-for-byte duplicate of assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-03/s52-oled-properties.png; source audit inherited.
The OLED layer stack and paired HOMO/LUMO energy diagram match Fig. 2 of the RSC article.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s07.caption: An ordered lattice supports coherent vibrational transport, while disorder increases scattering. Electrons are charged particles; phonons are quantized collective vibrations, and both can carry heat. Original source not identified.
evidence: Byte-for-byte duplicate of assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-03/s53-thermal-transport.jpeg; source audit inherited.
Compared semantic and reverse-image results for the two-panel lattice, spring, and thermal-wave diagram.
Only conceptually similar phonon and thermal-conductivity illustrations were found.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s08.caption: Magnetic classes distinguish parallel, alternating, partially cancelling, field-induced, and weak opposing arrangements of local moments. Original source not identified.

Diamagnetic and paramagnetic responses differ in electron pairing and in how an external field changes the local moment. Collective ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and ferrimagnetic order adds a second level beyond this local picture. Original source not identified.
evidence: Byte-for-byte duplicate of assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-03/s54-magnetic-classes.png; source audit inherited.
ChemDunn's comparison chart has the exact headings, iconography, and color scheme.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s10.caption: A unit cell may be chosen in several equivalent ways. A crystal model must give the same physical prediction after changing the cell origin, translating an atom through a boundary, or selecting another equivalent periodic representation.
A crystal structure combines a translation lattice with a basis of atoms. The finite pair is a compact representation of an infinite periodic point set.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s11.caption: The fourteen Bravais lattices enumerate distinct periodic translation structures. They do not specify the atoms in the basis, and the lecture emphasizes that a lattice type is not itself the full symmetry group of a decorated crystal.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s12.caption: Mirror and glide operations can look locally similar but differ by an accompanying translation. Such point-plus-translation operations are part of the full space-group symmetry.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s13.caption: Crystal systems constrain lattice geometry; Bravais lattices add translation and centering; point groups describe rotations, reflections, and inversion; space groups combine these ingredients with screw and glide operations.
The seventeen wallpaper groups are the two-dimensional analogue of the 230 three-dimensional space groups. They show why periodic translation alone does not determine the complete symmetry.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s14.caption: In the p4mm group, one representative point generates a symmetry orbit. A general site has the largest multiplicity, while special sites lie on symmetry elements and have fewer free coordinates. Original source not identified.

A Wyckoff table records each position's multiplicity, letter, site symmetry, and generated coordinates. A compact generative variable can therefore expand into a much larger orbit. Original source not identified.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s15.caption: Negative formation energy is not enough. A candidate is stable only when no combination of competing phases at the same overall composition lies below it on the convex hull.

Formation energy compares the assembled crystal with reference states of its constituent elements. The lecture's nucleation illustration connects that thermodynamic quantity to the physical act of forming a crystal.
evidence: Byte-for-byte duplicate of assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-03/s57-crystal-stability.jpeg; source audit inherited.
The separate atoms through euhedral-crystal growth sequence matches Fig. 4.7 of the open textbook.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s17.caption: Crystal structure prediction alternates proposal, local relaxation, scoring, and selection. A learned generator changes the proposal distribution so that more candidates begin near realistic crystal configurations.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s18.caption: DiffCSP jointly denoises lattice and fractional coordinates. Fractional coordinates encode periodicity directly, while the denoising model preserves rotation, translation, and equivalent periodic descriptions.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s19.caption: Explicit space-group constraints produce the largest match-rate gains on Carbon-24 and MPTS-52; the ground-truth-constraint row also exposes the remaining gap in symmetry prediction. Source: DiffCSP++.

DiffCSP++ constrains the lattice and coordinates during denoising rather than testing symmetry only after generation. Red arrows encode crystal-family lattice constraints; blue arrows encode Wyckoff-position constraints.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s20.caption: SymmCD treats the colored sector as an asymmetric unit. Diffusion acts on the compact representative, and the selected space-group operations determine how that representative fills the complete cell.
SymmCD's model state and reconstruction state are different objects. The network generates a small asymmetric unit; Wyckoff projection and group replication turn it into the full periodic crystal.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s22.caption: CDVAE separates global latent modeling from geometric decoding. The encoder compresses a crystal, prediction heads recover global attributes, and the score network iteratively denoises atomic structure.
Reconstruction quality varies across perovskites, carbon structures, and MP-20 crystals, showing that structural diversity matters beyond whether a decoder is generative. Source: CDVAE.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s23.caption: Match rate increases sharply when twenty candidates are allowed, while RMSE records the geometric fidelity of matched structures. Source: CrystaLLM.
CrystaLLM predicts a CIF one token at a time. A composition prompt starts the sequence; the model must continue with mutually consistent lattice, symmetry, species, and coordinate fields.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s24.caption: The benchmark separates syntactic and structural validity, coverage, property distribution, and metastability. Scaling improves some columns, but no single metric establishes experimental viability. Source: Gruver et al.
candidate_citations: • Gruver et al., finetunes LLaMa-70B to generate CIF files.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s24.caption: The model keeps CIF-like string representations but transfers an optimized pretrained language-model architecture. Data augmentation exposes equivalent textual descriptions of the same material. Source: Gruver et al.
candidate_citations: • Gruver et al., finetunes LLaMa-70B to generate CIF files.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s25.caption: The upper table evaluates composition-conditioned structure prediction; the lower table evaluates de novo composition-and-structure generation and reports integration cost alongside validity, coverage, stability, and uniqueness. Source: FlowMM.

FlowMM transports lattice, fractional coordinates, and atom types along different paths. Fractional coordinates live on a periodic torus, while atom types are represented continuously during transport and quantized at the endpoint.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s26.caption: MatterGen's generated examples span different compositions, coordination environments, and space groups. A broad chemical generator still hands each candidate to stability and property validation.

MatterGen first learns an unconditional crystal distribution, then inserts an adapter to condition generation on chemistry, symmetry, or a scalar property. The same geometric core network is reused across design objectives.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s27.caption: ADiT moves the shared modeling problem into latent space. One autoencoder vocabulary covers atom types, coordinates, cell information, and modality labels; a diffusion Transformer generates the latent representation.
The benchmark distinguishes validity from energetic stability and uniqueness. Joint molecule–material training improves several MP20 metrics relative to the material-only ADiT row. Source: ADiT.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s28.caption: Chemeleon aligns text and crystal embeddings, then injects the text condition into reverse diffusion. The prompt changes the generated distribution; it does not replace structural or energetic verification.

The Chemeleon examples move from a composition-level request to several candidate structures in the Ti–Zn–O system. Chemical rules and phase stability still decide which candidates merit calculation or synthesis.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s29.caption: Battery operation couples ionic transport through the electrolyte with electronic transport through electrodes and the external circuit. Each component therefore imposes a different material objective.
evidence: Byte-for-byte duplicate of assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-03/s65-battery-cell.png; source audit inherited.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s29.caption: A solid electrolyte must transport lithium ions while blocking electrons and remaining compatible with both electrodes. A plausible stable crystal is only one part of that requirement.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s30.caption: These four Li–P–S–Cl structures are candidate solid electrolytes. Their formulas and geometries define structures to test; they do not by themselves establish conductivity or synthesizability. Source: Chemeleon.
evidence: Byte-for-byte duplicate of assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-03/s66-chemeleon-candidates.png; source audit inherited.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s30.caption: The phase diagrams compare known and generated candidates across the Li–P–S–Cl system. Stability is relational: every candidate must be compared with competing phases at neighboring compositions.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s31.caption: LiFlow's downstream check is diffusivity, not visual trajectory quality. The plots compare estimates across temperature, chemical composition, trajectory source, and supercell size. Source: LiFlow.
LiFlow learns finite-time atomic displacements rather than one-step forces. The Propagator advances the state; the Corrector repairs local geometry before the next generated interval.
The trajectory comparison checks the time-ordered object that LiFlow generates. Similar endpoint structures alone would not establish the correct transport dynamics. Source: LiFlow.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s32.caption: Donor and acceptor doping control the mobile carrier type. The central depletion region forms when carriers diffuse across an n–p junction and leave ionized dopants behind.
evidence: Byte-for-byte duplicate of assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-03/s67-semiconductor-doping.jpeg; source audit inherited.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s32.caption: Substitutional lattice chemistry creates band-level carrier states. Phosphorus adds a donor electron near the conduction band; boron creates an acceptor level and a valence-band hole. Original source not identified.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s33.caption: The HfO split has a different distribution from SiN. Reporting the material and environment split is part of the scientific claim because force-field transfer depends on which local configurations were seen.
SAMD23 makes out-of-distribution structure explicit. Semiconductor simulation encounters amorphous networks, polymorphs, defects, surfaces, clusters, and molecules rather than one clean bulk lattice.

The SiN benchmark counts show that model evaluation covers different amounts of train, test, and OOD structure. The paper pairs these force metrics with simulation-derived checks rather than ranking models by one error alone.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s34.caption: The CTMT funnel quantifies attrition after generation. Only twenty of 104 topology-screened candidates pass the energetic, dynamical, and electronic verification chain.

CTMT assigns a different scientific question to each stage: generation, structural validity, heuristic topology, energetic stability, phonon stability, and final topological classification. No one model output answers all six.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s35.caption: A heterogeneous reaction is a sequence of surface configurations. Adsorption, surface reaction, and desorption depend on the local atomic geometry of the slab and the adsorbate.
evidence: Byte-for-byte duplicate of assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-03/s68-heterogeneous-catalysis.jpeg; source audit inherited.

assets/img/blog/lectures/gdl-2025-21/s36.caption: AdsorbDiff predicts a rigid adsorbate placement, then delegates local relaxation and energy verification to separate models. Success is defined after this full pipeline, not at the raw diffusion output.

Open Catalyst Project structures expose the diversity hidden by the phrase 'adsorbate on a slab.' Elemental composition, facet, local coordination, adsorption site, and molecular orientation all change the relaxed energy.
AdsorbDiff is much stronger with one proposal; additional proposals narrow and eventually reverse the comparison with AdsorbML. Source: AdsorbDiff.

assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-05/.caption: QM9 associates molecular geometries with a broad set of scalar quantum-chemical targets. The data set is described by Ramakrishnan et al.
MD17 and revised MD17 sample molecular conformations along quantum-mechanical trajectories. Revised labels and trajectory statistics are documented by Christensen and von Lilienfeld.
Molecular dynamics needs directional information: forces act on individual atoms and must follow a rotated molecular geometry. The energy-gradient construction is central to NequIP.
Traditional force fields separate pair, angular, torsional, and nonbonded contributions. That hierarchy motivates the directional features introduced by DimeNet and extended by GemNet.

Compatibility of composition is the operational content of a group action: applying two rigid motions in sequence must equal applying their group product. This representation language is used systematically in Cohen and Welling's steerable CNNs.
The two paths end at the same object: first acting by g' and then by g agrees with the single action of gg'. See Cohen and Welling for the corresponding representation-based construction.
Circular harmonics separate angular signals into frequencies. A spatial rotation changes the phase within one frequency pair but does not mix different frequencies, as formalized in steerable CNNs.
Spherical harmonics organize angular functions by degree ℓ and component m. Color records sign, while lobes reveal the increasing angular frequency used by Tensor Field Networks.
Rotating an angular function steers each fixed-ℓ coefficient vector by its Wigner D matrix. This is the angular transformation law used by Thomas et al.

Equivariance means that transforming the input before the model gives the same result as transforming the model's output afterward. EGNN realizes this relation with invariant messages and equivariant coordinate differences.

Pair distances, three-body angles, and four-body dihedrals expose progressively richer local geometry while avoiding an arbitrary global orientation; GemNet develops the corresponding two-hop construction.
A grid-bound filter produces stepwise changes as an atom crosses cells; SchNet's continuous radial filter changes smoothly with position. From Schütt et al.
Angular energy changes continuously with a three-atom geometry, motivating the explicit angle channel introduced by DimeNet.
A torsional potential is periodic and distinguishes conformations that pair distances alone may represent awkwardly. This directional motivation is explicit in DimeNet.
The directed message (m_{ji}) aggregates incoming bond messages (m_{kj}) and the angle between the two directions. From Gasteiger et al.
The torsion φ measures the rotation between the two bond planes of H₂O₂, completing the local description used by GemNet beyond distances and bond angles.
GemNet couples the neighborhoods on both ends of a bond so that its message can depend on two bond angles and their relative rotation. From Gasteiger, Becker, and Günnemann.
A nine-component rank-two Cartesian tensor decomposes into irreducible blocks of dimensions 1, 3, and 5: trace, antisymmetric, and symmetric traceless. See the tensor discussion in Duval et al.
A Clebsch–Gordan array contracts two input component axes into an output component while respecting the allowed representation types used in Tensor Field Networks.
Successive Cartesian orders occupy blocks whose dimensions grow as 1, 3, 9, and so on, before the irreducible decomposition reviewed by Duval et al.

assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-05/.caption: A basis change reorganizes the same nine Cartesian entries into ℓ=0, ℓ=1, and ℓ=2 blocks. From Duval et al.
An edge direction is normalized onto the sphere and expanded in spherical harmonics, producing one typed geometric feature for each degree. This is the angular construction of Thomas et al.
A TFN feature tensor separates location (a), channel (c), degree ℓ, and component (m). The example stores velocities and accelerations as separate type-one channels. From Thomas et al.
TFN alternates typed convolutions, within-type channel mixing, and admissible nonlinearities before reducing to invariant type-zero outputs. From Thomas et al.

Gaussian conditional flow matching separates path choice, velocity target, boundary conditions, and regression loss. Source: Neklyudov et al. (2024), Flow Matching: A Guide and Code.

The tangent plane contains the locally available linear directions at one point on the sphere. Exact visual source unclear.
A geodesic follows the curved state space rather than the straight chord through its ambient space. Exact visual source unclear.
The exponential map follows a tangent vector along its geodesic to a point on the manifold. Exact visual source unclear.
The logarithmic map returns a manifold point to a tangent displacement at the chosen base point. Exact visual source unclear.

Machine-learning potentials aim to combine electronic-structure accuracy with force-field efficiency across molecules, materials, and biomolecules.
A two-dimensional dihedral map summarizes recurrent conformations and barriers visited by the trajectory.
Learned collective variables compress atomistic configurations into a low-dimensional landscape for analysis.
Dihedral angles provide compact coordinates for rotations around molecular bonds.
Binding free energies can be organized through a thermodynamic cycle connecting solvated and complexed states.
The folding landscape contains many intermediate conformations and barriers between unfolded and native basins.
Atomistic trajectories reveal how mobile species move through a host material.
Spatial coarse-graining maps atomistic configurations to fewer variables, learns coarse interactions, and decodes coarse trajectories.

Temporal coarse-graining replaces many small integration steps with a longer-lag transition model. [Timewarp](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/a598c367280f9054434fdcc227ce4d38-Abstract-Conference.html) uses such long proposals inside an equilibrium-correct MCMC chain.
Coarse-graining replaces groups of atoms with effective interaction sites.
Integrating out atomistic detail can smooth a landscape and make longer numerical steps possible.
Metadynamics progressively fills visited basins with bias potential along a chosen collective variable.
Replica exchange couples simulations at several temperatures through accepted state swaps.
Temperature annealing broadens the sampled distribution and increases barrier-crossing probability.

Neural coarse-graining learns reduced interactions and, in some methods, a distribution over compatible atomistic backmaps. See [chemically transferable generative backmapping](https://openreview.net/forum?id=7DnvWyVkUo).

A long-lag proposal can replace many sequential MD updates while an acceptance step preserves the equilibrium target, as in [Timewarp](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/a598c367280f9054434fdcc227ce4d38-Abstract-Conference.html).
[MDGen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.17808) compares generated paths through structural states, free-energy surfaces, and trajectory-level statistics.
[MDGen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.17808) represents a molecular trajectory as a sequence that can be generated, infilled, upsampled, or extrapolated by changing the conditioning pattern.
[LiFlow](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42256-025-01125-4) advances an atomic displacement distribution with a propagator and corrects local geometries with a second model.
candidate_citations: Nam, Juno, et al. "Flow matching for accelerated simulation of atomic transport in materials." arXiv preprint arXiv:2410.01464 (2024).

An unbiased trajectory spends most of its time inside metastable basins and rarely visits the transition region.

assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-09/.caption: A molecular generator can sit inside a structure-based design loop in which the user specifies a target environment and inspects proposed ligands. See the [Chemistry42 platform paper](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.jcim.2c01191).

Practical molecular design combines generation with scoring, filtering, and human decisions; the generator is one component of a larger search loop. See the [Chemistry42 platform paper](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.jcim.2c01191).
Graph generation fits a model distribution to observed examples and samples new graphs from it. Lecture diagram by the author.

GraphRNN's two recurrent levels mirror its nested grammar: one state advances the graph, while another emits the new node's edges. See [You et al., 2018](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/you18a.html).

Breadth-first ordering concentrates many graph edges near the adjacency-matrix diagonal, reducing the edge generator's practical look-back horizon. See [You et al., 2018](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/you18a.html).
An adjacency-matrix grammar specifies the graph through atom and bond entries; the neural generator must learn consistency across the matrix. Lecture diagram by the author.
The matrix is only a representation of the underlying graph; reindexing its nodes changes the matrix without changing the graph. Lecture diagram by the author.

A motif vocabulary promotes recurring subgraphs from many atom-level actions into reusable construction units. See the hierarchical motif formulation of [Jin et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.03230).
Motif generation advances through chemically meaningful fragment attachments rather than individual adjacency entries. See [Jin et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.03230).
Large molecular structures often contain repeated subgraphs, making fragment-level actions much shorter than atom-by-atom construction. Lecture examples by the author.

SMILES records a graph through a traversal, so one molecular graph can have several valid serializations. The exact origin of this illustrative panel is unclear; [Daylight's SMILES theory page](http://www.daylight.com/dayhtml/doc/theory/theory.smiles.html) documents the notation.
String generation converts molecular construction into next-token prediction, followed by deterministic parsing back to a graph. Lecture diagram by the author.
Graph diffusion denoises an entire graph state rather than committing to one node-addition history. The exact origin of this animation is unresolved.
GDSS defines stochastic forward and reverse processes jointly over node features and adjacency variables. See [Jo et al., 2022](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/jo22a.html).
Separate but coupled score networks estimate denoising directions for node and edge variables. See [Jo et al., 2022](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/jo22a.html).
GraphARM learns a discrete node ordering for masking and reconstructs categorical graph states in reverse. See [Kong et al., 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kong23b.html).
Retrosynthesis systems combine one-step precursor prediction with recursive route planning and evaluation. From the review by [Zhong et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.05864).
Forward prediction resolves products from reactants, whereas retrosynthesis proposes precursor sets from a target product. Lecture diagram by the author.

CGLN combines learned graph representations with explicit transformation logic for template-based retrosynthesis. See [Dai et al., 2019](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/9090-retrosynthesis-prediction-with-conditional-graph-logic-network).

Reaction templates encode recurring local bond changes that can be applied backward to a target molecule. See the [Conditional Graph Logic Network](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/9090-retrosynthesis-prediction-with-conditional-graph-logic-network).
G2Gs separates template-free retrosynthesis into reaction-center identification and synthon completion. See [Shi et al., 2020](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/shi20d.html).
A variational graph decoder translates product-derived synthons into one or more precursor graphs. See [Shi et al., 2020](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/shi20d.html).

Root alignment chooses compatible SMILES traversals so the translation model spends less capacity learning arbitrary token reordering. See [Zhong et al., 2022](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2022/sc/d2sc02763a).
Chimera merges candidates from complementary retrosynthesis models and learns a common ranking over their union. See [Maziarz et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05269).
The ensemble improves ranked precursor prediction because its components contribute different correct reactions. See [Maziarz et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05269).
Different component models localize and express useful disconnections differently, creating diversity for the ensemble. See [Maziarz et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05269).

ElemwiseRetro frames inorganic retrosynthesis as elementwise precursor selection from literature recipes. See [McDermott et al., 2024](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2024/sc/d3sc03538g).
candidate_citations: Kim, Seongmin, et al. "Predicting synthesis recipes of inorganic crystal materials using elementwise template formulation." Chemical Science 15.3 (2024): 1039-1045.

assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-09/.caption: Retro* embeds a learned one-step model and value estimate inside iterative tree search for complete synthetic routes. See [Chen et al., 2020](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/chen20k.html).

Amortized tree generation learns to emit complete retrosynthetic structures instead of invoking a separate search procedure at inference time. See [Liu et al.](https://openreview.net/forum?id=FRxhHdnxt1).
FlowER represents a reaction through electron redistribution rather than only a before-and-after graph pair. See [Irwin et al., 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09426-9).

A mechanistic sequence records electron and bond changes that mediate the molecular graph transformation. See the [mechanistic reaction dataset](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-024-03709-y) and [FlowER](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09426-9).

ChemCrow augments a language model with chemistry-specific tools, separating conversational planning from specialist computation and retrieval. See [Bran et al., 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42256-024-00832-8).
MolT5 shares a sequence model across molecular strings and natural language, enabling translation in both directions. See [Edwards et al., 2022](https://aclanthology.org/2022.emnlp-main.26/).

ReactionT5 uses a common sequence interface for several reaction tasks, with pretraining intended to help when task-specific reaction data are limited. See [Sagawa and Kojima](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.06708).

Chemeleon aligns text and crystal representations, then uses the aligned text embedding to guide diffusion over composition and periodic structure. See [Park et al., 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-59636-y).

assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-11/.caption: Atomic orbitals are one-electron functions, whereas the exact molecular wavefunction depends jointly on every electron coordinate. The embedded graphic credits HowStuffWorks (2001); the exact page is unclear.
A wavefunction can change sign across a node, but its electron density is nonnegative because it depends on the squared magnitude. Exact visual source unclear.
Orbitals provide lower-dimensional ingredients from which approximate many-electron states can be assembled. Exact composite source unclear.
The Born--Oppenheimer approximation exploits the mass and time-scale separation between nuclei and electrons. Exact visual source unclear.
Evaluating orbitals at all electron positions produces a matrix whose determinant supplies the required fermionic sign change. Exact animation source unclear.
Two electrons may share a spatial orbital only with opposite spins; duplicating the same spin orbital is forbidden. Exact visual source unclear.
FermiNet replaces fixed orbitals with neural functions of the complete electron configuration. Exact animation source unclear.
The variational challenge is concentrated in the small correlation-energy remainder beyond the dominant mean-field energy. Exact visual source unclear.

FermiNet lowers variational energy errors across atoms and molecules by learning a more expressive antisymmetric ansatz. Source: Pfau et al. (2020), Ab-initio Solution of the Many-Electron Schrödinger Equation with Deep Neural Networks.

PsiFormer uses self-attention to exchange information among electrons before assembling the antisymmetric wavefunction. Source: von Glehn, Spencer & Pfau (2022), A Self-Attention Ansatz for Ab-initio Quantum Chemistry.
PsiFormer converges to lower reported energies than FermiNet on the larger atomic and molecular systems shown. Source: von Glehn, Spencer & Pfau (2022).

Orbformer amortizes wavefunction learning across molecules before fine-tuning on a target chemical process. Source: Foster et al. (2025), An ab initio foundation model of wavefunctions that accurately describes chemical bond breaking.

A joint neural-state objective supports vertical excitation energies, oscillator strengths, double excitations, and conical-intersection calculations. Source: Pfau et al. (2024), Accurate Computation of Quantum Excited States with Neural Networks.
Density functional theory replaces the many-electron state with a three-dimensional ground-state density. Exact diagram source unclear.
Kohn--Sham DFT replaces the interacting solve with noninteracting orbitals constrained to reproduce the same density. Exact visual source unclear.
A Kohn--Sham calculation is a fixed-point iteration because its density is both an input to and an output of the Hamiltonian. Lecture diagram by the author.
Jacob's ladder orders density-functional approximations by the information they use and the accuracy-cost regime they target. Exact visual source unclear.

Skala learns an exchange-correlation contribution from density features, using wavefunction-theory energies as supervision. Source: Luise et al. (2025), Accurate and scalable exchange-correlation with deep learning.
Skala converts density features into local representations, communicates across grid points, and integrates the resulting energy density. Source: Luise et al. (2025).
The functional is evaluated on spatial integration points carrying learned density features. Source: Luise et al. (2025).
Self-consistent fine-tuning evaluates the learned functional on its own iterated densities instead of only on frozen reference densities. Lecture diagram by the author.
Skala combines low W4-17 atomization-energy error with a broader GMTKN55 evaluation against conventional functionals. Source: Luise et al. (2025).
Self-consistent fine-tuning reduces reaction-energy and dipole errors produced by the densities that Skala itself induces. Source: Luise et al. (2025).
A subset-level audit reveals which reaction, barrier, interaction, and conformer regimes contribute to the aggregate GMTKN55 score. Source: Luise et al. (2025).

QHNet predicts the structured Hamiltonian produced by a DFT calculation and evaluates matrix, eigenvalue, acceleration, and orbital-similarity errors. Source: Yu et al. (2023), Efficient and Equivariant Graph Networks for Predicting Quantum Hamiltonian.

QHFlow transports structured matrix priors toward geometry-conditioned Hamiltonians, then tests the result through density, orbital energies, and SCF acceleration. Source: Kim et al. (2025), High-order Equivariant Flow Matching for Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian Prediction.

DeepDFT treats density as a coordinate-query function: atom nodes exchange messages, while probe nodes receive local information and output charge density. Source: Jørgensen & Bhowmik (2020), DeepDFT.
Plane waves represent global variation, while Gaussian-type orbitals concentrate resolution near nuclei. Source: Kim & Ahn (2024), Gaussian Plane-Wave Neural Operator for Electron Density Estimation.
GPWNO predicts a global field representation, so evaluating density does not require a fresh graph-network pass at every coordinate. Source: Kim & Ahn (2024).
Atom-centered and virtual bond-centered Gaussian fields provide a compact basis for localized and bonding density. Source: Fu et al. (2024), A Recipe for Charge Density Prediction.

assets/img/blog/lectures/ml4mol-2025-12/.caption: Protein function spans enzymes, transporters, antibodies, and therapeutic molecules.
Modern protein design combines progress in predicting structures, representing sequences, and generating both sequences and backbones.
Programmable design asks for a sequence that realizes a specified function, with stability, expression, and structural uncertainty remaining part of the problem.
The sequence representation records the ordered amino-acid polymer.
The twenty residue types share a backbone but differ in side-chain chemistry.
Protein structure connects sequence to local motifs, a folded chain, and multichain assemblies.
A protein geometry consists of a common backbone plus chemically distinct side chains, with torsion angles controlling local conformation.
A folded protein is an ensemble concentrated around several minima rather than one perfectly rigid coordinate set.
Functional protein motion can connect distinct macroscopic conformations, as illustrated by an ABC transporter cycle.
Template-based modeling and physical simulation supply complementary routes to protein structure and dynamics.
Large sequence and structure repositories make data-driven protein modeling possible.
Different protein tasks operate on one-dimensional sequence, evolutionary alignments, three-dimensional structures, or time-dependent ensembles.
One-dimensional models turn residue sequences into representations for property prediction and sequence design.
Three-dimensional encoders use geometric and graph structure to learn residue- or atom-level representations.
Structure prediction combines one-dimensional and pairwise information to produce three-dimensional coordinates.
Protein ensemble models predict a distribution over structures rather than one coordinate set.
Sequence design operates on residue identities, either unconditionally or under structural constraints.
Inverse folding and motif-conditioned design connect a desired geometry back to a compatible sequence.
Three-dimensional generative models expand design from choosing residues to proposing new protein geometries.
Structure prediction is useful because protein geometry and motion constrain biological function.
The AlphaFold series marks successive changes in prediction target, architecture, and representation.
Backbone torsions describe local conformation without fixing a global coordinate frame.
Pairwise distance distributions provide global structural constraints that complement local torsions.
AlphaFold1 treats residue pairs as a two-dimensional feature map processed by convolutional blocks.
Pair features turn residue identities and evolutionary relations into a grid on which the model predicts geometry.
An MSA collects homologous sequences so the model can use conservation and covariation as structural evidence.
Coevolving columns can reveal residues whose geometric or functional relationship is conserved through evolution.
Conservation and correlated variation supply constraints beyond the query sequence alone.
Mapping covariance back to three dimensions links evolutionary statistics to structural proximity and function.
Small local torsion errors can create large global displacement when coordinates are reconstructed sequentially.
AlphaFold1 is a model-and-solver system: learned geometric distributions define an energy optimized over structure.
A predicted distance distribution becomes a differentiable structural potential evaluated at candidate coordinates.
AlphaFold1 delegates coordinate construction to optimization, whereas AlphaFold2 and 3 make coordinate prediction part of the learned model.
Learned distance potentials are supplemented by physical restraints that discourage atom overlap.
AlphaFold1's CASP13 result demonstrated the strength of learned geometric potentials combined with structural optimization.
AlphaFold2 predicts a rigid frame per residue for the backbone and torsions for side-chain geometry.
Residue-wise frames turn coordinate prediction into coupled translation, rotation, and torsion updates.
Residue frames provide a structured coordinate representation between an atom cloud and the full fold.
Relative frame geometry contains directional information that a distance matrix alone cannot express.
AlphaFold2 couples evolutionary reasoning, pairwise geometric reasoning, coordinate generation, and recycling in one end-to-end architecture.

Row attention is conditioned on the residue-pair state rather than treating the alignment as an isolated sequence matrix.
Column attention aggregates how different homologs realize the same aligned position.
Triangle operations let the pair representation reason about geometric consistency through a third residue.
The outgoing triangle update aggregates paths from one residue through an intermediate residue to another.
Incoming and outgoing variants encode the two orientations of a directed triangle update.
Triangle attention weighs alternative intermediate residues when refining each pair relation.
The updated pair tensor is fed back into MSA attention in the next Evoformer cycle.
A pair-derived bias directly modifies the softmax logits of MSA attention.
Column attention preserves the alignment axis that distinguishes homologous sequences from residue positions.
The outer-product mean converts aligned sequence covariation into an explicit residue-pair update.
Averaging over homologs creates a pairwise statistic that complements direct pair and template features.
The structure module converts abstract sequence and pair states into a full coordinate model.
IPA performs attention using points expressed in residue-local frames, coupling learned features to three-dimensional geometry.
Structure refinement alternates geometric attention, feature transitions, and rigid-frame updates.
FAPE evaluates coordinate error after expressing atoms in local residue frames.
AlphaFold2's frame-based structure module respects global rotations and translations of its geometric input.
Recycling lets AlphaFold2 repeatedly reconcile its sequence, pair, and coordinate representations.
AlphaFold2's CASP14 performance established end-to-end learned coordinate prediction as a new reference point.
AlphaFold-Multimer generalizes residue and pair reasoning to assemblies containing several protein chains.

CellPLM promotes each spatially located cell to a token in a tissue-level model. Source: [Wen et al. (2024)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/173bcdbd820edbe43284e0941109ada9-Abstract-Conference.html).

CellPLM aggregates each cell's gene expression, models interactions among cell tokens, and decodes masked or noisy profiles from a tissue-level latent space. Source: [Wen et al. (2024)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/173bcdbd820edbe43284e0941109ada9-Abstract-Conference.html).

The learned spatial cell representation supports tissue reconstruction and prediction tasks. Source: [Wen et al. (2024)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/173bcdbd820edbe43284e0941109ada9-Abstract-Conference.html).
GEARS uses gene relationships to extrapolate from observed interventions to unseen perturbation combinations. Source: [Roohani et al. (2023)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-023-01905-6).

Evaluation asks whether the graph-guided model predicts held-out combinations rather than only repeated single-gene effects. Source: [Roohani et al. (2023)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-023-01905-6).

TxPert encodes a control-cell expression state, adds a perturbation embedding derived from a biological knowledge graph, and decodes the perturbed expression profile. Source: [Wenkel et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.14919).

Tahoe-x1 conditions a large single-cell model on chemical perturbations represented by Morgan fingerprints. Source: [Gandhi et al. (2025)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.10.23.683759v1).

The evaluation compares general and context-specific essential-gene prediction, making the cellular context part of the target rather than a nuisance variable. Source: [Gandhi et al. (2025)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.10.23.683759v1).
Tahoe-x1 tests whether larger perturbation-trained models improve several cellular tasks. Source: [Gandhi et al. (2025)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.10.23.683759v1).
The evaluation spans both response prediction and more general cell representation tasks. Source: [Gandhi et al. (2025)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.10.23.683759v1).
PerturbQA turns perturbation knowledge into a question-answering benchmark for language models. Source: [Wu et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.21290).
The benchmark measures whether a model can reason over cell state, intervention, and response evidence. Source: [Wu et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.21290).
SynthPert distills synthetic perturbation reasoning traces into a specialized model. Source: [Phillips et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25346).

SynthPert is compared with physical, graph, single-cell, retrieval, and fine-tuned language-model baselines on differential expression and direction-of-change prediction. Source: [Phillips et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25346).
Synthetic-trace fine-tuning is evaluated against other language-model baselines. Source: [Phillips et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25346).

Cell2Sentence supports conditional cell generation, cell-label prediction, and natural-language interpretation by formatting each task as a prompt-response pair. Source: [Levine et al. (2024)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/levine24a.html).
Cell2Sentence evaluates whether the serialization preserves useful cell-state information. Source: [Levine et al. (2024)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/levine24a.html).
Cell2Sentence serializes an expression profile as a gene-token sentence for language-model fine-tuning. Source: [Levine et al. (2024)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/levine24a.html).
The textual interface lets a language model perform cell annotation and expression-conditioned generation. Source: [Levine et al. (2024)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/levine24a.html).

Cell2Sentence-Scale trains a common language interface over expression-derived sentences and biomedical text. Source: [Gemma Team et al. (2025)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.04.14.648850v4).

Reinforcement learning extends the scaled model from representation learning toward interactive cellular reasoning. Source: [Gemma Team et al. (2025)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.04.14.648850v4).

The scaled model is tested across biological question answering, state interpretation, and expression-grounded tasks. Source: [Gemma Team et al. (2025)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.04.14.648850v4).

Capability profiles compare performance across several cell-language tasks rather than one aggregate score. Source: [Gemma Team et al. (2025)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.04.14.648850v4).

The system connects cell serialization, biomedical language modeling, and reinforced response generation. Source: [Gemma Team et al. (2025)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.04.14.648850v4).
